newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay shares end lower, political worries remain.
newsitem.headline: Bombay shares end lower, political worries remain.

text.p: ** Bombay shares finish 1.45 percent lower
in a day of nervous, choppy trade
** Benchmark stocks index down 52.98 points, or 1.45
percent, to provisional close of 3,597.90
** Congress party orders its lawmakers in parliament to
vote against Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda in a
confidence motion due on Friday
** United Front coalition says Congress has given it until
3 p.m. (0930 GMT) to respond to its demand that Prime
Minister H.D. Deve Gowda step down, but offers no
comments after deadline
Bombay blue chips ended lower in nervous trade on Thursday with market players awaiting political developments, dealers said.
The ruling United Front coalition, which is in a minority in parliament, faces a vote of confidence on Friday.
Stocks dipped on news the Congress party had instructed its deputies to vote against the ruling coalition in the vote but the political situation remained unclear, dealers said.
"Yes, there is confusion, but everybody is hopeful that there will be some way out," Brij Gopal Daga, chief general manager (market operations) at Unit Trust of India told Reuters.
The Congress decision to vote against the government, after two rounds of talks was bad news for the market, but traders said they were still hopeful of a patch-up.
"The market came off, but is off its lows. Perhaps, most people are still not convinced about the news," Prashant Purker, head of institutional sales at Peregrine Securities said.
"The market thinks there is still hope for conciliation."

The Congress on March 30 withdrew crucial support for Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's 15-party centre-left coalition sparking off the current political crisis and raising the prospect of mid-term elections.
Senior United Front leader Laloo Prasad Yadav on Thursday said India will have to hold fresh general elections as talks with the Congress party had failed.
"Read my lips. There will be elections. Let the people decide," Laloo told reporters in New Delhi after the Congress deadline had expired.
The Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) is open for trading on Saturday between 10:00 a.m. and 1:30 p.m. (0430-0800 GMT) because of political developments, the BSE said on Thursday.
-- Anshuman Daga, Bombay equities desk +91-22-265 9000
